summary: Targeted closing check of the v3 series: earlier findings resolved, edits introduce no new errors

resolved: Commit 1, round-3 unverified nit ("changes nothing for a valid v0.9 payload"): the sentence now says that a `hidden` resolving to null is added, which matches the code (the `'hidden': BehaviorNode(Behavior.dynamic)` shape entry) and the updated test `_expectReadOnlyNull(accessibility['hidden'])`. A small residue is reported above as a nit.
Commit 1, round-3 unverified nit (CHANGELOG conflict when ported): no change needed. Its own fix said so, and the conflict is a keep-both resolution.

Commit 2, round-3 confirmed should-fix and Astra finding 1 (the fallback is all or nothing): v3 narrows the message to "When the arguments fail with every replacement made, they are all checked again with none made ... still matches, unless another value in the same call needs the replacement." The argumentErrors doc now says "or else with none replaced". Probe at 5a3c5c0b with a custom v1.0 `echo` taking {flag: boolean, status: object{valid, note}}: flag only and status only each match, and both together throw at #root["flag"]. That is exactly what the message now says.

Commit 2, round-3 confirmed should-fix (`grouping` given a validation result is read as truthy): fixed in code. functions.dart passes `ValidationResult.validityOf(args['grouping']) ?? args['grouping']` for formatNumber and formatCurrency, and the message, the CHANGELOG and the function-map doc now say so. I probed it at 5a3c5c0b with v10.invoke and value 1234567. grouping false, ValidationResult(valid:false), {valid:false} and {valid:false, severity:'warning'} all give 1234567 and $1234567.00. true, absent, ValidationResult(valid:true) and {valid:true, message} all give 1,234,567 and $1,234,567.00. {valid:'no'} and {other:1} still fail with EXPRESSION_ERROR, because the check only replaces a boolean `valid`. Through expression resolution, grouping {@path} on {valid:false} gives 1234567, grouping required('') gives 1234567, and grouping not(required('')) gives 1,234,567. v0.9 is unchanged: grouping false gives 1234567, and {valid:false} still raises EXPRESSION_ERROR. In the v1.0 catalog's functions, `grouping` is the only DynamicBoolean argument besides those of and/or/not. The function-map doc's "a map carrying a `valid` key" matches validityOf, which reads any map with a `valid` key as `valid == true`. basic_catalog_test.dart and catalog_json_test.dart pass, and `dart analyze --fatal-infos lib` is clean at 5a3c5c0b. The new unit test calls `execute` directly, so it skips the argument check, but the invoke path is the one I probed.

Astra finding 4 (custom functions still receive objects): deliberately left. The message states the behaviour and the reason: "Only the check uses the replacement: the function receives each argument as it was resolved" and "Passing plain booleans to functions ... would need the coercion directed by each argument's schema." The CHANGELOG tells catalog authors the same: "The function still receives each argument as it was resolved". The probe confirms that `echo` receives the ValidationResult unchanged.

Commit 2's new message text follows the author's rules: no semicolons, no padded em dashes, ends with ⚠️ Agent-generated, and has no Co-Authored-By. Its claims ("since a validation result can now reach it", that v0.9 replaces nothing, that a ValidationResult is checked as its JSON object on every catalog) match the code.

problems.title: argumentErrors still reports a valid ValidationResult operand as an error when the call fails, and neither the doc nor the message says so (round-3 unverified nit, still open)
problems.evidence: On a v1.0 catalog, when both passes fail, `argumentErrors` returns the errors of the pass with nothing replaced. Probe at 5a3c5c0b: `v10.invoke('and', {'values': [ValidationResult(valid: true), 5]}, ctx)` throws `... matched 0 at path #root["values"]["0"]; Expected to match exactly one schema, but matched 0 at path #root["values"]["1"]`, so it blames values[0], which the replacement accepted. The doc says it returns "The ways [args] fail [fn]'s argument schema". Neither the message nor the doc says that the reported errors come from the check with nothing replaced, so this round-3 nit is neither fixed nor left with a reason.
problems.fix: Either return the errors of the replacement pass when both fail on a v1.0 catalog (`final List<ValidationError> replaced = ...; if (replaced.isEmpty) return replaced;` ... `return replaced;` after the second pass also fails), or add to the doc comment: "When both checks fail, the errors returned are those of the check with none replaced."

problems.title: Commit 1's v0.9 sentence dropped the "absent" qualifier, so it is false for a v0.9 payload that carries `hidden`
problems.evidence: The message says: "v0.9 defines no `hidden`, so for a v0.9 payload this only adds a `hidden` that resolves to null." The v0.9 AccessibilityAttributes in specification/v0_9/json/common_types.json has no `additionalProperties: false`, and a component whose schema leaves out `accessibility` does not check it at all. So a v0.9 payload `{"accessibility": {"hidden": true}}` now reaches node.props as a binding to `true` instead of the raw `true` that the old static shape passed through. It does not resolve to null. The round-3 fix said "an absent `hidden`", and v3 left that word out.
problems.fix: "v0.9 defines no `hidden`, so for a v0.9 payload, which carries none, this only adds a `hidden` that resolves to null."

problems.title: Markdown stripping nits 12 and 13 still present, with no reason stated
problems.evidence: text.dart L96 `_codeSpan = RegExp(r'`([^`\n]+)`')` runs before `_escape`, and L58 matches `_heading` (L77, `^ {0,3}...`) against `text.trim()`. The message says escapes are kept literal, and does not say these corners are accepted. Both are edge cases of best-effort stripping.
problems.fix: Either use `text.trimRight()` (or strip only line breaks) before `_heading`, and `RegExp(r'(?<!\\)`([^`\n]+)`')` for `_codeSpan`, with test cases, or add one bullet to the message's Choices: "Stripping is best effort: an escaped backtick pair can still read as a code span, and an indented `#` line still reads as a heading."

problems.title: Commit 11 says the v0.9 and, or and not read a {"valid": ...} object as truthy, but the v0.9 argument check rejects that object first
problems.evidence: New v3 sentence: "This differs from the v0.9 `and`, `or` and `not`, which read such an object as truthy." Since commit 2 (5a3c5c0b), `argumentErrors` replaces nothing on a v0.9 catalog, and the v0.9 `and`/`not` args are DynamicBoolean (specification/v0_9/catalogs/basic/catalog.json). So a `{"valid": ...}` operand fails the argument check and never reaches the function body. Commit 2's own test pins this: basic_catalog_test.dart `'a v0.9 invoke checks a result object as an object'` expects `v09.invoke('not', {'value': {'valid': false}}, ...)` to throw `A2uiExpressionError`. Only the body's `isTruthy` (function_support.dart:74) would read a map as truthy, and no payload reaches it. Commit 2's message uses the same wording as a hypothetical ("would pass an operand the function then reads as truthy"). Commit 11 states it as current behavior.
problems.fix: Replace the sentence with: "This differs from the v0.9 `and`, `or` and `not`, whose argument check rejects such an object."

votes.reasoning:
I tried to refute this and could not. Commit 0e51cf7e says: "This differs from the v0.9 `and`, `or` and `not`, which read such an object as truthy." It states this as current behaviour, but no payload can reach that behaviour.

1. **The v0.9 argument check rejects the object first.** In `data_context.dart:1200-1216`, `argumentErrors` makes the validity replacement only when `protocolVersion.isAtLeast(v1_0)`. On v0.9 it checks with `validity: false`, so a `{"valid": false}` map is checked as an object.
2. **The v0.9 schema does not accept an object like that.** The arguments of `and`, `or` and `not` are DynamicBoolean (`specification/v0_9/catalogs/basic/catalog.json`). DynamicBoolean is a oneOf of boolean, DataBinding or FunctionCall (`common_types.json:147`), and `{"valid": false}` matches none of them.
3. **Both execution paths run that check first.** `Catalog.invoke` (`data_context.dart:1164-1173`) throws `A2uiExpressionError` before `fn.execute`. The RPC handler (`rpc_handler.dart:392-403`) throws `invalidFunctionCall` before `fn.execute`. Those are the only two `.execute(` calls in a2ui_core/lib or a2ui_flutter/lib.
4. **Commit 2's test pins the rejection.** `basic_catalog_test.dart:458`, 'a v0.9 invoke checks a result object as an object', expects `v09.invoke('not', {'value': {'valid': false}}, ...)` to throw `A2uiExpressionError`.

**What does read the map as truthy:** the function bodies, called directly. The test at `basic_catalog_test.dart:487` ('v0.9 treats a {valid} map as a plain, truthy object') does this through `_call`, which calls `catalog.functions[name]!.execute` and skips `invoke`. That is the only sense in which the sentence holds. Commit 2's message is careful about this: it frames the truthy reading as what would happen ("would pass an operand the function then reads as truthy"). Commit 11 drops that framing and reads as a description of what v0.9 does with such a payload today, which is wrong. A payload gets EXPRESSION_ERROR, not truthy.

**Why should-fix and not blocker:** the claim is literally true of the bodies, and the code is unaffected. But a reader would come away with the wrong idea of what v0.9 does with such a payload.

**Fix:** use the proposed sentence: "This differs from the v0.9 `and`, `or` and `not`, whose argument check rejects such an object."

Confirmed. The new sentence in commit 11 (0e51cf7e) says: "This differs from the v0.9 `and`, `or` and `not`, which read such an object as truthy." At 0e51cf7e and at HEAD 8c25c42a, an object like that never gets to those function bodies.

How I checked (I read the code and the existing test, but did not run anything):
- **Argument check runs first on both call paths.** In `dart/a2ui_core/lib/src/resolution/data_context.dart`, `invoke` (L1164-1173) calls `argumentErrors` and throws `A2uiExpressionError` before `fn.execute`. The RPC path in `rpc_handler.dart` (L392-403) does the same check before `fn.execute`. These are the only two callers of `.execute(` in `a2ui_core/lib`.
- **No replacement on v0.9.** `argumentErrors` (L1204-1210) replaces values only when `protocolVersion` is at least v1_0. On v0.9 the check uses `_checkable(validity: false)`, which leaves a `{'valid': ...}` map as it is.
- **The v0.9 schema rejects the object.** In `specification/v0_9/catalogs/basic/catalog.json`, the `not` arg `value` and the `and`/`or` `values.items` are all `$ref ... DynamicBoolean`, so the map fails the check.
- **A test pins this.** `basic_catalog_test.dart` L458-468, "a v0.9 invoke checks a result object as an object", expects `v09.invoke('not', {'value': {'valid': false}}, ...)` to throw `A2uiExpressionError`. The test is still present at HEAD.
- **Only unreachable code reads it as truthy.** The `isTruthy` in `function_support.dart` L74 would read a map as truthy, but no payload gets there. Commit 2's message (5a3c5c0b) words this as a hypothetical ("would pass an operand the function then reads as truthy"). Commit 11 states it as current behaviour.

So a porter reading commit 11 would think a v0.9 `not({"valid": false})` evaluates to false. It actually fails with EXPRESSION_ERROR.

On severity: the brief's own scale lists "a wrong claim" under blocker. The false claim here is a side contrast, though, and the rest of the commit (the code, the test and the core rule it describes) is accurate, so should-fix is a fair grade. Either way the problem is real.

The proposed fix is accurate: "This differs from the v0.9 `and`, `or` and `not`, whose argument check rejects such an object."

problems.title: Commit 1's new v0.9 sentence ignores a v0.9 payload that writes hidden itself
problems.evidence: v3: "v0.9 defines no `hidden`, so for a v0.9 payload this only adds a `hidden` that resolves to null." The v0.9 AccessibilityAttributes schema (specification/v0_9/json/common_types.json) is not closed, so a v0.9 payload may carry `hidden`. On a component whose schema leaves out `accessibility`, a written `hidden`, bound or literal, is now resolved instead of passing through raw. Commit 12 (8c25c42a) acknowledges the same case: "a v0.9 payload that writes one as a literal gets it."
problems.fix: "v0.9 defines no `hidden`, so for a v0.9 payload that sets none this only adds a `hidden` that resolves to null."

problems.title: Commit 10's Button doc comment went back to "While a check fails it is disabled", which the commit's own severity split makes imprecise
